questions.q: After Josiah died, who became king of Jerusalem?
questions.a: The people of the land made Josiah’s son, Jehoahaz, king and he reigned for three months.

questions.q: How did Eliakim become king of Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.a: His brother, the king of Egypt, removed Jehoahaz after three months and made Eliakim king, changing his name to Jehoiakim.

questions.q: What kind of ruler was Jehoiakim in his reign of eleven years?
questions.a: Jehoiakim was evil in the sight of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did King Nebuchadnezzar, of Babylon, do to the king of Judah?
questions.a: He attacked him, bound him in chains, and took him to Babylon.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar do to the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: He carried some of the objects in the house of Yahweh to Babylon, and put them in his palace.
His son, Jehoiachin, became king after him.

questions.q: What kind of king was Jehoiachin?
questions.a: In his short reign, he did evil in the sight of Yahweh.

questions.q: How did King Nebuchadnezzar treat this Jehoiachin?
questions.a: He brought Jehoiachin to Babylon along with more valuable things from the house of Yahweh.

questions.q: How did Zedekiah respond to Yahweh?
questions.a: He did evil in the sight of Yahweh, and he did not humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah, who spoke from the mouth of Yahweh.

questions.q: How did Zedekiah rebel against King Nebuchadnezzar?
questions.a: He hardened his heart against Yahweh and turned away from King Nebuchadnezzar.

questions.q: How did the people respond to the compassion that Yahweh continued to show them?
questions.a: They mocked God’s messengers, despised his words, and scoffed at his prophets.

questions.q: How did God deal with the mockers?
questions.a: He had the young men killed by the king of the Chaldeans, and all the others were given over to the king.

questions.q: What did the king of the Babylonians do to Jerusalem and what did he take to Babylon?
questions.a: He destroyed the house of God, the wall of Jerusalem, all its palaces, and the beautiful things in it. Then he took all the furnishings and treasures to Babylon.

questions.q: What happened to those that escaped the killing?
questions.a: They became servants for the king and his sons, which fulfilled Yahweh’s words to Jeremiah.

questions.q: What did Cyrus, king of Persia, proclaim and put in writing?
questions.a: He said Yahweh had commanded him to build a house of God in Jerusalem and that God would be with them when they go up to the land.

commentary.text: Verses 1–21 The ruin of Judah and Jerusalem came on by degrees. The methods God takes to call back sinners by his word, by ministers, by conscience, by providences, are all instances of his compassion toward them, and his unwillingness that any should perish. See here what woful havoc sin makes, and, as we value the comfort and continuance of our earthly blessings, let us keep that worm from the root of them. They had many times ploughed and sowed their land in the seventh year, when it should have rested, and now it lay unploughed and unsown for ten times seven years. God will be no loser in his glory at last, by the disobedience of men. If they refused to let the land rest, God would make it rest. What place, O God, shall thy justice spare, if Jerusalem has perished? If that delight of thine were cut off for wickedness, let us not be high-minded, but fear.

God had promised the restoring of the captives, and the rebuilding of Jerusalem, at the end of seventy years; and that time to favour Zion, that set time, came at last. Though God's church be cast down, it is not cast off; though his people be corrected, they are not abandoned; though thrown into the furnace, they are not lost there, nor left there any longer than till the dross be separated. Though God contend long, he will not contend always. Before we close the books of the Chronicles, which contain a faithful register of events, think what desolation sin introduced into the world, nay, even into the church of God. Let us tremble at what is here recorded, while in the character of some few gracious souls, we discover that the Lord left not himself without witness. And when we have looked at this faithful portrait of man by nature, let us contrast with it that same nature, when recovered by Almighty grace, through the justifying and soul-adorning righteousness of Christ our Saviour.
